## Alpha diversity

### Shannon indices 

As a proxy for alpha diversity we calculate the Shannon diversity index of each sample for the bacterial, fungal and oomycete communities.

```{r}
#| label: Shannon diversity
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

# Calculate Shannon index using the vegan package
bSHANNON <- diversity(t(bCOUNT), index="shannon")
fSHANNON <- diversity(t(fCOUNT), index="shannon")
oSHANNON <- diversity(t(oCOUNT), index="shannon")

# Print the calculated Shannon diversity indices
#print(bSHANNON)
#print(fSHANNON)
#print(oSHANNON)
```

### Differences in alpha diversity between lines and conditions

We analyse for differences in bacterial alpha diversity between the different Arabidopsis lines and conditions using a two-way ANOVA with the model: *shanon-index ~ lines \* conditions* followed by a Post-hoc Tukey's HSD test.

```{r}
#| label: Shannon diversity statistics - fuction
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

analyze_shannon_diversity <- function(count_table, design_table, label = "Microbiome", test="ANOVA") {
  library(dplyr)
  library(knitr)

  # Step 1: Compute Shannon diversity
  shannon <- vegan::diversity(t(count_table), index = "shannon") %>% as.data.frame()
  colnames(shannon) <- "shannon"
  shannon <- shannon %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "sample_name")

  # Step 2: Merge with metadata
  merged_data <- merge(shannon, design_table, by = "sample_name")
  merged_data$condition <- as.factor(merged_data$condition)
  merged_data$line <- as.factor(merged_data$line)

  # Step 3: Two-way ANOVA
  anova_model <- aov(shannon ~ condition * line, data = merged_data)
  anova_results <- summary(anova_model)

  # Step 4: Tukey's HSD post-hoc
  posthoc_results <- TukeyHSD(anova_model)

  # Step 5: Output
  if(test=="ANOVA"){
      anova_table <- as.data.frame(anova_results[[1]])
      return(kable(anova_table, caption = paste0(label, ": ANOVA"),
        col.names = c("Df", "Sum Sq", "Mean Sq", "F Value", "Pr(>F)")))

  }
  if(test=="Tukey"){
      tukey_table <- as.data.frame(posthoc_results$`condition:line`)
      tukey_table <- tibble::rownames_to_column(tukey_table, var = "Comparison")
      return(kable(tukey_table, caption = paste0(label, ": Tukey HSD"),
        col.names = c("Comparison", "Diff", "Lower", "Upper", "p-value")))
  }
}

```

```{r}
#| label: shannon diversity statistics bacteria
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

analyze_shannon_diversity(bCOUNT, bDESIGN, "Bacteria", test = "ANOVA")
analyze_shannon_diversity(bCOUNT, bDESIGN, "Bacteria", test = "Tukey")

```

### Alpha diversity - plot

```{r}
#| label: plot shannon diversity function
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false
#| fig-width: 9  # Adjust figure width
#| fig-height: 5  # Adjust figure height




plot_shannon_diversity <- function(count_table, design_table, title_label = "Microbiome") {

  # Compute Shannon diversity
  shannon <- vegan::diversity(t(count_table), index = "shannon") %>% as.data.frame()
  colnames(shannon) <- "shannon"
  shannon <- rownames_to_column(shannon, var = "sample_name")

  # Merge with metadata
  merged_data <- merge(shannon, design_table, by = "sample_name")
  merged_data$condition <- as.factor(merged_data$condition)
  merged_data$line <- as.factor(merged_data$line)

  # Plot
  p <- ggplot(
    merged_data, 
    aes(x = line, y = shannon, fill = condition, alpha = line)
  ) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
    geom_point(
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.75),
      size = 1.5,
      color = "black",
      aes(color = condition, shape = line)
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.5),
      text = element_text(size = 7),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 7),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 7),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Shannon index -", title_label),
      x = "Condition", 
      y = "Shannon index",
      fill = "Condition", 
      color = "Condition", 
      alpha = "Line"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = level_cols_condition) +
    scale_color_manual(values = level_cols_condition) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(0.9, 0.5)) +
    expand_limits(y = 0) +  # Ensures Y-axis starts at 0
    stat_compare_means(
      method = "kruskal.test", 
      label = "p.signif",
      label.y = max(merged_data$shannon, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.8
    )

  return(p)
}

bSHANNON_plot <- plot_shannon_diversity(bCOUNT, bDESIGN, "Bacteria")
fSHANNON_plot <- plot_shannon_diversity(fCOUNT, fDESIGN, "Fungi")
oSHANNON_plot <- plot_shannon_diversity(oCOUNT, oDESIGN, "Oomycetes")

# Combine all three figures
SHANNON_plot <- plot_grid(
  bSHANNON_plot + theme(legend.position = "none"),
  fSHANNON_plot + theme(legend.position = "bottom"),
  oSHANNON_plot + theme(legend.position = "none"),
  align = "hv", 
  nrow = 1
)
SHANNON_plot

ggsave(
  filename = "alpha_diversity_plot.pdf", 
  plot = SHANNON_plot, 
  width = 16.5, 
  height = 7, 
  units = "cm", 
  path = "Output/figures/"
)



```

## Beta diversity

### Bray-Curtis distances

We get an overview of the community structure by calculating Bray-Curtis (BC) distances as proxy for beta diversity between all samples for the bacterial, fungal and oomycete communities. 

### Differences in beta diversity between lines and conditions

We investigate the full model to see which factors alters the beta diversity by performing a PERMANOVA using the model: *BC ~ lines \* conditions* and visualize our findings by ploting the first two axes of a unconstrained PCoA and a constrained CAP (model: *BC ~ lines \* conditions*).

```{r}
#| label: PERMANOVA
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
#| paged-print: false


set.seed(100010)

#Bacteria
bdist <- vegdist(t(bCOUNT), method="bray")
bdist_paov <- adonis2(bdist ~ line * condition, by = "terms", data=bDESIGN)
kable(bdist_paov, caption = "Bacteria: PERMANOVA",
      col.names = c("Term", "DF", "Sums of Squares", "Mean Squares", "F-Model", "P-Value"))

#Fungi
fdist <- vegdist(t(fCOUNT), method="bray")
fdist_paov <- adonis2(fdist ~ line * condition, by = "terms", data=fDESIGN)
kable(fdist_paov, caption = "Fungi: PERMANOVA",
      col.names = c("Term", "DF", "Sums of Squares", "Mean Squares", "F-Model", "P-Value"))

#Oomycetes
odist <- vegdist(t(oCOUNT), method="bray")
odist_paov <- adonis2(odist ~ line * condition, by = "terms", data=oDESIGN)
kable(odist_paov, caption = "Oomycetes: PERMANOVA",
      col.names = c("Term", "DF", "Sums of Squares", "Mean Squares", "F-Model", "P-Value"))

```

**Conclusion:** The bacterial communities are different between the different Arabidopsis-lines, and the interaction between lines and condition. No community alteration was detected for fungi while we find a difference between the conditions for oomycetes.


```{r}
#| label: Pairwise PERMANOVA
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

library(vegan)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)

# Function to run pairwise PERMANOVA and display with kable
run_pairwise_permanova <- function(count_data, design_data, group_label = "Group") {
  pairwise_results <- list()

  # Ensure sample order matches
  count_data <- count_data[, design_data$bc_ID]

  # 1. WT vs 318 at each condition
  for (cond in unique(design_data$condition)) {
    sub_design <- design_data %>% filter(condition == cond)
    sub_data <- t(count_data[, sub_design$bc_ID])
    dist <- vegdist(sub_data, method = "bray")
    result <- adonis2(dist ~ line, data = sub_design)
    pairwise_results[[paste0("Line_", cond)]] <- result
  }

  # 2. plus vs minus within each line
  for (ln in unique(design_data$line)) {
    sub_design <- design_data %>% filter(line == ln)
    sub_data <- t(count_data[, sub_design$bc_ID])
    dist <- vegdist(sub_data, method = "bray")
    result <- adonis2(dist ~ condition, data = sub_design)
    pairwise_results[[paste0("Condition_", ln)]] <- result
  }

  # Display all results
  for (name in names(pairwise_results)) {
    cat("\n\n")
    cat(paste0("### ", group_label, ": ", gsub("_", " ", name), "\n\n"))
    print(
      kable(pairwise_results[[name]],
            caption = paste(group_label, "- PERMANOVA:", gsub("_", " ", name)),
            col.names = c("Term", "DF", "Sums of Squares", "Mean Squares", "F-Model", "P-Value"),
            digits = 4)
    )
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: Pairwise PERMANOVA output
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

# Bacteria
run_pairwise_permanova(bCOUNT, bDESIGN, "Bacteria")

# Fungi
run_pairwise_permanova(fCOUNT, fDESIGN, "Fungi")

# Oomycetes
run_pairwise_permanova(oCOUNT, oDESIGN, "Oomycetes")
```

##  PCoA - line and condition effect on beta diversity

```{r}
#| label: centroid line function
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

#function to get centroid lines
centroid_lines <- function(PHYSEQ, dist_matrix, group, axes=c(1,2)){
  #get ordination values
  lines <- as.data.frame(plot_ordination(PHYSEQ, dist_matrix, axes=axes, justDF=T))
  colnames(lines)[1:2] <- c("Axis.1","Axis.2")
  lines <- lines[,colnames(lines) %in% c("Axis.1","Axis.2",group)]#subset
  #get centroids (means of each group)
  means1 <- aggregate(lines$Axis.1, by=as.list(lines[,colnames(lines) %in% group, drop=F]), FUN=mean)
  means2 <- aggregate(lines$Axis.2, by=as.list(lines[,colnames(lines) %in% group, drop=F]), FUN=mean)
  #concat groups (for multiple groups)
  lines$concact <- lines[,colnames(lines) %in% group,drop=F] %>% apply(2, as.character) %>% apply(1, paste, collapse="")
  means1$concact <- means1[,colnames(means1) %in% group,drop=F] %>% apply(2, as.character) %>% apply(1, paste, collapse="")
  means2$concact <- means2[,colnames(means2) %in% group,drop=F] %>% apply(2, as.character) %>% apply(1, paste, collapse="")
  #add means to COUNTa.frame
  lines$Axis.1.means <- NA
  lines$Axis.2.means <- NA
  group_values <- unique(lines$concact)
  for (i in group_values) {
    lines$Axis.1.means[lines$concact == i] <- means1$x[means1$concact == i]
    lines$Axis.2.means[lines$concact == i] <- means2$x[means1$concact == i]
  }
  #subset df
  lines <- lines[,colnames(lines) %in% c("Axis.1","Axis.2","Axis.1.means","Axis.2.means")]
  #return
  return(lines)
}

```

```{r}
#| label: PCoA
```

## CAP - line and condition effect on beta diversity

```{r}
#| label: CAP plot
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false
#| fig-width: 9  # Adjust figure width
#| fig-height: 4  # Adjust figure height

# Function to process and plot CAP
process_CAP <- function(PHYSEQ, dist_paov, title, colors) {
  CAP_bray <- ordinate(PHYSEQ, method = "CAP", formula = ~ line * condition, distance = "bray")
  
  # Use full PHYSEQ, no subsetting by phylum
  score <- paste(
    " ~ line * condition \n line: ",
    format(dist_paov$R2[rownames(dist_paov) == "line"] * 100, digits = 2, nsmall = 1),
    "% var, P=", format(dist_paov$`Pr(>F)`[rownames(dist_paov) == "line"], digits = 2),
    "\n condition: ",
    format(dist_paov$R2[rownames(dist_paov) == "condition"] * 100, digits = 2, nsmall = 1),
    "% var, P=", format(dist_paov$`Pr(>F)`[rownames(dist_paov) == "condition"], digits = 2),
    "\n line:condition: ",
    format(dist_paov$R2[rownames(dist_paov) == "line:condition"] * 100, digits = 2, nsmall = 1),
    "% var, P=", format(dist_paov$`Pr(>F)`[rownames(dist_paov) == "line:condition"], digits = 2)
  )

  p0 <- phyloseq::plot_ordination(PHYSEQ, CAP_bray, title = title, axes = c(1, 2))
  p0$layers <- p0$layers[-1]
  p0 <- p0 +
    stat_ellipse(
      geom = "polygon", type = "t", level = 0.95, size = 0.4,
      aes(group = condition, color = condition, fill = condition), 
      alpha = 0.01
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
    ggnewscale::new_scale_color() +
    geom_point(aes(shape = factor(line), color = condition), size = 1.0) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 2)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
    labs(
      subtitle = score,
      color = "Microbiome", fill = "Microbiome", 
      shape = "Line", alpha = "Line"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      text = element_text(size = 7),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 7),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 7),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7)
    )
  return(p0)
}

# ==============================
# Create plots 
# ==============================


fig_bac <- process_CAP(bPHYSEQ, bdist_paov, "Bacteria", level_cols_condition)
fig_fun <- process_CAP(fPHYSEQ, fdist_paov, "Fungi", level_cols_condition)
fig_oom <- process_CAP(oPHYSEQ, odist_paov, "Oomycetes", level_cols_condition)

# ==============================
# Combine and Save Plots ---------------------------
# ==============================

# Combine all three figures
fig_5.2 <- plot_grid(
  fig_bac + theme(legend.position = "none"),
  fig_fun + theme(legend.position = "none"),
  fig_oom + theme(legend.position = "none"),
  align = "hv", 
  nrow = 1
)

# Extract legend from the Bacteria plot

# Add legend to the combined plot
CAP_plot <- plot_grid(fig_5.2, legend, nrow = 2, rel_heights = c(1, 0.1))

print(CAP_plot)

# Print and save
ggsave(
  "CAP_condition_color.pdf", 
  plot = CAP_plot, 
  width = 17.5, 
  height = 8, 
  units = "cm", 
  path = "Output/Figures/"
)

```

\vspace{5mm}

**Conclusion:** Even though we find difference between line and condition, we see that they can explain only a small percent of the community structures.The largest effect is between WT and mmf1-2 mutants on the BXplus soil.
